newsitem.title: USA: USDA budget should be shielded from cuts - lawmakers.
newsitem.headline: USDA budget should be shielded from cuts - lawmakers.

text.p: The head of the House Agriculture Committee and some 100 members of Congress urged federal budget writers to leave farm spending intact, citing $60 billion in agriculture cuts in the past decade and savings from last year's Freedom to Farm legislation.

Oregon Republican Bob Smith, the chairman of the agriculture committee, and Charles Stenholm of Texas, the committee's ranking Democrat, said in a letter to Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich, R-Ohio, that spending had already been cut more deeply than other areas of the budget.

"The contribution of the agriculture sector to budget savings over the past 12 years, in percentage terms, far exceeds any other major budget function," the letter said. "No other area of the budget has so consistently made such major contributions to budget control during this period."
The letter was supported by 100 other members of Congress .
Congress adopted farm legislation last year that removed most federal controls over agriculture, and capped annual subsidy spending on program commodities.
The Clinton Administration's proposed budget called for total USDA spending of $58.7 billion, an increase of $1.8 billion from the last fiscal year.
